topics.title: The AI-washing con: why half of "AI layoffs" aren't actually about AI
topics.why: New data shows nearly 6 in 10 companies admit framing cuts as AI-driven when the real driver is financial — timely because it changes how readers should interpret every scary layoff headline this year.

topics.title: Companies that fired workers for AI are quietly rehiring them
topics.why: A rehiring boomerang is showing up in 2026 data as AI hits a 60%-of-duties ceiling — the workers getting rehired reveal exactly which skills make you hard to replace.

topics.title: 79% of companies say adopting AI is tearing them apart — and that's the opening
topics.why: Fresh 2026 enterprise survey data shows a huge gap between AI investment and ROI, which is exactly the gap that AI-adoption-savvy knowledge workers can get paid to close.

topics.title: The bifurcation is here: 'force multiplier' professionals vs. everyone else
topics.why: 2026 labor-market research describes a small tier of people who direct AI agents at department-level output — worth naming precisely what moves someone into that tier.

topics.title: What Blind and Reddit say about 2026 layoffs that press releases don't
topics.why: With ~80k tech layoffs already this year and heavy AI-or-overhiring debate on Blind/Reddit, there's a practical playbook in how insiders read these announcements versus how PR frames them.
